summary.text: Riley Owen, a Republican U.S. Navy Reserve intelligence officer in his twenties from Salt Lake City, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Utah's open 1st Congressional District to Ben McAdams.

He says he was a White House political appointee on trade and manufacturing policy before working in the shipbuilding, critical minerals and drone industries, and he won the nomination at the April 2026 Republican convention.

paragraphs.text: Riley Owen says he comes from six generations of Utahns. He lives in Salt Lake City and was 27 when he announced his campaign, according to KSL.
He studied international relations at Princeton University, graduating with High Honors, and was an Eisenhower Scholar at Oxford University, where he earned a Master of Public Policy with Merit.

Owen served as a White House political appointee working on trade and manufacturing policy; KUER describes him as a former Trump White House staffer. After government service he worked in industry in shipbuilding, critical minerals and drones, and Ballotpedia also lists CEO among his career experience.
He serves as an intelligence officer in the U.S. Navy Reserve.
Owen won the Republican nomination outright with 71.2% of the delegate vote at the April 25, 2026 Utah Republican convention, so no Republican primary was held.
He told KUER he was focusing on affordability, business tax credits for paid maternity leave, and housing.
During the campaign, he said he was running to defend children and families and to stop career politicians.
He received 26.2% of the vote to Ben McAdams's 70.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
